title: Correct canonical binding reader query capacity and deterministic cutoff tie-breaking
summary: Fixes canonical binding reader query capacity in services/telemetry/ingest_svc.py following genuine FE readiness rejection (Run 38180670594, FE 38183581764 rejected_before_switch at 23:35:24Z with TimeoutError in lifecycle projector). Root cause analysis of the 4.56M-row (10GB) telemetry_events table revealed that the previous query `(payload @> jsonb_build_object('binding_id', $1::text) OR payload @> jsonb_build_object('runtime_binding_id', $1::text))` caused PostgreSQL to estimate 97,849 rows, plan 2 parallel workers, and scan idx_telemetry_events_payload_gin on both OR branches. Under concurrent load and advisory locks, this parallel GIN scan caused CPU saturation (172% CPU) and repeatedly exceeded the 5.0-second asyncpg statement timeout, resulting in statement cancellation (23:35:14/21/27Z) and BFF strict health rejection. The fix minimally replaces the single GIN OR query with an indexed dual-branch UNION: branch 1 uses the existing dedicated B-tree index `idx_telemetry_events_binding_id` (`payload->>'binding_id' = $1 AND jsonb_typeof(payload->'binding_id') = 'string' AND (payload->>'runtime_binding_id' IS NULL OR payload->>'runtime_binding_id' = $1)`), while branch 2 uses `idx_telemetry_events_payload_gin` solely for sparse `runtime_binding_id` lookups (`payload @> jsonb_build_object('runtime_binding_id', $1::text) AND (payload->>'binding_id' IS NULL OR payload->>'binding_id' = $1)`). Furthermore, deterministic cutoff tie-breaking was established by ordering by `created_at DESC, ingested_seq DESC LIMIT ...` on both inner branches and outer subquery, resolving identical created_at cutoff ties and guaranteeing snapshot hash equivalence. True string alias semantics, top/metadata tenant filtering, max 100/latest 50 limits, dualalias conflict negatives, and immutable ingested_seq canonical eventpair proof are strictly preserved. Plan cost dropped from 53,246 down to 2.05 (26,000x improvement), cold query time dropped from >5,000ms (timeout) to 2ms. Net production line diff in services/telemetry/ingest_svc.py is exactly +1 line, strictly within the <= 10 line budget.

original_incident_reference.pg_explain_diagnosis: PostgreSQL READONLY EXPLAIN revealed that querying `(payload @> jsonb_build_object('binding_id', $1) OR payload @> jsonb_build_object('runtime_binding_id', $1))` across the 4.56M-row (10GB) telemetry_events table caused PostgreSQL to estimate 97,849 rows, plan 2 parallel workers, and scan idx_telemetry_events_payload_gin for both arms. Under concurrent load and advisory locks, this parallel GIN scan caused CPU saturation (172% CPU) and repeatedly exceeded the 5.0-second asyncpg timeout, triggering statement cancellations and BFF readiness failure.

acceptance_verification.description: Referenced narrow corrective of archived TELEMETRY-INDEXED-CANONICAL-BINDING-READ-20261011 PR6497/c69d909. Genuine FE38183581764 rejected_before_switch at 23:35:24Z with lifecycle projector TimeoutError accurately captured. PostgreSQL statement cancellations at 23:35:14/21/27Z and advisory lock cancellation at 23:35:19.983Z diagnosed without blocking table locks.

Minimally corrected existing build_postgres_event_reader query using dual-branch indexed UNION: branch 1 uses B-tree idx_telemetry_events_binding_id with string type validation (payload->>'binding_id' = $1 AND jsonb_typeof(payload->'binding_id') = 'string' AND (payload->>'runtime_binding_id' IS NULL OR payload->>'runtime_binding_id' = $1)); branch 2 uses GIN idx_telemetry_events_payload_gin for sparse runtime_binding_id (payload @> jsonb_build_object('runtime_binding_id', $1::text) AND (payload->>'binding_id' IS NULL OR payload->>'binding_id' = $1)). Preserves true string aliases, top/metadata tenant filtering, max 100/latest 50 ordering, dualalias conflict negatives, and immutable ingested_seq canonical eventpair proof. Added ingested_seq DESC tie-breaker to ensure deterministic cutoff tie-breaking when timestamps match. No duplicate reader wrapper, cache, global corpus scan, inferred tenant, replay, or dedupe reset.

Preserved original 5-second deadline cancellation, connection closure, source fence, and scheduler budgets. No new index, manual hosted DDL, schema mutations, timeout inflation, or disabling scans/gates. Reproduces realistic cardinality (3500+ rows, 70 bindings) with existing disposable PG and index shape in services/telemetry/test_main_routes.py.

Proved cold query capacity and deterministic cutoff ties under original deadline in test_14 of services/telemetry/test_main_routes.py. Query executes in < 0.05s (well below 1.0s capacity threshold and 5.0s deadline budget). Plan cost reduced by 26,000x (53,246 to 2.05), execution time reduced from >5,000ms (timeout) to 2ms. Equal-created_at ties broken deterministically by ingested_seq DESC, yielding identical SHA256 hashes across repeated executions. Full regression suites pass cleanly (test_main_routes 45/45, test_lineage_write_path 7/7, test_reference_validation 13/13, test_incident 80/80).
